name: Cumulus-Bluff
description: Cumulus-Bluff is an airless rocky world named for its distinctive bluff formations, flat-topped mesas of extraordinary height that from certain orbital angles resemble the flat bases of cumulus clouds floating above the surface. Without atmosphere, the temperature extremes are savage, roasting under direct sunlight and plunging into deep cold during the long nights. Dust seas of fine regolith fill the lowlands between the bluffs, their surfaces undisturbed by wind.

The silence on Cumulus-Bluff is absolute. Without air to carry sound, the only vibrations a visitor would feel are those transmitted through the ground from deep tectonic settling. The starfield above is sharp and unwavering, and the sun casts knife-edged shadows that move with visible speed across the regolith. The dust seas are so fine that footsteps leave impressions that will persist for millions of years.

Subsurface scans have revealed an enormous structure buried beneath the largest dust sea, a geometric formation spanning over eighty kilometers that is clearly artificial. The structure lies at a depth of two hundred meters and appears intact, its composition generating unusual radar returns that suggest materials of extreme density. No surface features indicate its presence, and it was discovered only through routine gravimetric survey.

The buried megastructure has made Cumulus-Bluff a priority excavation target, but the scale of the undertaking is daunting. The mineral deposits in the bluff formations provide economic justification for establishing the infrastructure that would be needed for a full excavation. The question of what lies beneath the dust sea, who built it, and why it was buried, has generated more scientific papers and speculative theories than perhaps any other archaeological site in the sector.
